_comment: Instafill.ai product captions, for a screen recording rather than a social short. Four deliberate departures from red-card.json, which was measured off somebody else's channel and reads as a news chyron: (1) the slab is near-black at 12% transparency instead of saturated red -- a screen demo is already a busy, mostly-white frame, and a red bar competes with the very UI the video is pointing at, while a dark one recedes behind it; (2) sentence case, not uppercase -- a tutorial that shouts is a tutorial nobody finishes, and mixed case carries word shape, which is what makes a line readable at a glance; (3) the spotlight is the brand mint #13BA82, the same token config/cards/brands/instafill.json and the lower third use, so captions, a name label and an end card on one film read as one channel; (4) narrower lines and fewer words per group, because the frame under them is content the viewer needs to see.

overlays._note: Colour of the SOURCE video's own lower-third graphics to dodge, not the colour of this card. A screencast has none, so there is nothing to dodge.

_geometry.target: 1280x720 screen recording with a round webcam bubble in the bottom-left corner
_geometry.why_bottom_margin_96: 96 on the 1920 canvas scales to 64px at 720p, which puts the card's baseline clear of the Windows taskbar (top edge ~y 682) without pushing it up into the page content.
_geometry.why_max_line_1080: 1080 on the 1920 canvas scales to 720px at 720p, centred on x=640, so the card spans x 280..1000 and never reaches the webcam bubble at x<190. Widening this past ~1150 makes them collide.
